sources.hint: Manage local folders, USB/internal disks, SMB shares and CD ripping.
sources.none: No sources yet. Add one below.
sources.usbNeedsFormat: No recognized filesystem — format it from a computer.
sources.smbRw: Allow writing (needed to use it as a CD-rip destination)
sources.fsExt4Hint: Best choice for internal appliance storage.
sources.fsExfatHint: Readable from Windows/macOS if the disk is removed.
sources.warnBody: All data on {model} ({size}, {path}) will be permanently erased. This cannot be undone.
sources.keepPowered: Keep the appliance powered on until this finishes.
sources.doneAdopted: Disk formatted and added as a source
sources.doneHint: Copy your music to the network share below, then apply & rescan the library.
sources.needOsUpdate: A system update is required to enable network sharing (Samba) for internal disks.
sources.smbRegenerateHint: If Windows keeps rejecting the credentials, remove the saved entry for this device in Windows Credential Manager, then try again.
sources.subpathSaved: Subfolder saved — the library is being updated.
sources.localSambaHint: Also share this folder over the network (SMB), so you can copy music onto it from a PC.
sources.playlistdirHint: Where Lyrion saves the playlists you create from the player. The default works for most setups — pick a folder on your own disk if you'd rather keep the playlists next to your music.
sources.autoApplyHint: Every change is applied on its own — the library updates without restarting playback.
sources.addSourceHint: Network share, internal disk or a folder on this player
sources.shareHint: Folders this player publishes on the network, so you can copy music onto it from a computer.
sources.smbAltHostHint: If the player's IP address changes, use the name {host} in place of the address.
sources.smbHowtoIntro: Copy music onto "{name}" from any computer on the same network. The player must be switched on.
sources.smbHowtoWin1: Open File Explorer, click the address bar, type {path} and press Enter.
sources.smbHowtoWin2: When Windows asks for credentials, enter the username and password above and tick "Remember my credentials".
sources.smbHowtoWin3: To keep it handy, right-click the folder and choose "Map network drive…", ticking "Reconnect at sign-in": it will then appear under This PC at every start-up.
sources.smbHowtoMac1: In the Finder choose Go → Connect to Server (⌘K).
sources.smbHowtoMac3: Choose "Registered User", enter the username and password above, and tick "Remember this password in my keychain".
sources.smbHowtoMac4: The folder opens in the Finder and stays under Locations in the sidebar.
sources.smbHowtoMacTip: To mount it automatically at every login, add the mounted volume under System Settings → General → Login Items.

tailscale.hint: Join this appliance to your own Tailscale network (tailnet) so you can reach it — web UI, Lyrion Music Server, network shares, everything — from anywhere your tailnet reaches, e.g. to get at your music library away from home. This is not a public link: only devices on your own tailnet can reach it.
tailscale.unavailable: Tailscale isn't installed on this device yet.
tailscale.loginHint: Open this link on any device (even your phone) to approve this appliance from your own Tailscale account. Only needed the first time — the device stays authenticated after that.
tailscale.openLink: Open the link to approve this device

lyrion.hint: This device can run its own Lyrion Music Server, or use one that is already running on your network.
lyrion.internalHint: Lyrion Music Server runs on this device and manages your library.
lyrion.externalHint: Pick a Lyrion server already running on your network, or type its address.
lyrion.channelWarning: Nightly and development builds are pre-release: expect the occasional bug. Switch back to Release at any time.
lyrion.installFailed: The Lyrion installation failed. Check the connection and try again.
lyrion.skinHint: The look of Lyrion's web player (the page you open from a browser or phone). Osmium matches this device's interface.
lyrion.skinUnset: No skin chosen yet — this device still uses Lyrion's stock look. Pick one to switch.
lyrion.skinFailed: Could not apply the skin. Check the network connection and try again.

playback.help: Playback options applied to the active player: track transitions (crossfade/gapless), volume normalisation (ReplayGain), and fixed-volume (bit-perfect) output.
playback.noPlayer: No active player found. Start playback on the device or check the Lyrion connection.
playback.fixedVolumeHelp: Bypasses the player's digital volume control entirely — output is always at 100%. Required for bit-perfect playback; turn it off to use the on-screen volume slider again.
playback.autoExpandHelp: When a song starts playing, automatically open the fullscreen now-playing view after this many seconds. It only opens once per song — if the kiosk is navigated away manually, it stays put.
playback.vuMeterHelp: The VU dial in the "now playing" screen updates live with the audio level. Turn it off to reduce GPU load. Useful here because it's reachable even on a headless unit, where nobody has the on-screen settings open.

display.switchToOnscreen: Turn the on-screen interface back on
display.confirmHeadless: The device screen will turn off immediately. Continue?
display.changeFailed: Could not change the display mode
display.resolutionHelp: On large screens the interface is drawn at full panel resolution, which keeps the graphics chip busy. Rendering it lower and letting the screen enlarge it makes everything much smoother, at the cost of some sharpness.
display.confirmResolution: The device's interface will close and reopen after a few seconds. Playback is not interrupted. Continue?
display.refreshHelp: Both the screen scaling and the interface's own redraws are tied to the panel's refresh rate, so lowering it reduces graphics-chip load — roughly 40% less on this hardware. Applies immediately, no restart.
display.refreshUnsupported: This device's screen does not offer a lower refresh rate to switch to.
display.confirmRefresh: The device screen will switch to a lower refresh rate. Continue?
display.refreshChangeFailed: Could not change the refresh rate
display.pointerHelp: Show the mouse pointer on screen, or hide it if you only use the touchscreen. Shown by default, so the on-screen setup wizard stays usable.
display.pointerUnavailable: Pointer control is not available on this device.
display.playerHelp: Turn the player itself off for a server-only unit — Lyrion Music Server and everything else keeps running, this device just never plays audio locally. Useful for a box in a closet driving other players elsewhere.
display.confirmPlayerOff: This device will stop playing audio locally. Lyrion Music Server and remote control keep working. Continue?
display.playerChangeFailed: Could not change the player on/off state

timezone.hint: A fresh install has no way to ask for this, so it defaults to UTC — pick the device's real one here.

updates.confirmProdToDev: Once you update to a dev release, you will only be able to switch back to production once a production release newer than that dev release is out.
updates.keepPowered: The update continues on the device even if you close this page. Just keep it powered on.

companion.hint: Scan the QR code from the Osmium Sound Companion app to pair your phone.

companionIos.hint: On iPhone/iPad, use LyrPlay — a free App Store app for controlling Lyrion/Squeezebox: native FLAC/Opus decoding, real background playback, lock-screen controls, CarPlay and Siri. Scan the QR code to download it. Note: DSP, updates, reboot and multiroom role stay manageable only from the device screen and this web interface.
companionIos.open: Open LyrPlay on the App Store
companionIos.disclaimer: LyrPlay is a third-party app, not developed by or affiliated with this project. It is only recommended as a compatible Lyrion/Squeezebox client.

backup.hint: Save the device's configuration, Lyrion preferences and playlists. Set a passphrase to also include credentials (Wi-Fi, SMB shares, this web-admin account) in an encrypted, restorable file — without one, only non-secret settings are saved.
backup.passphraseHint: Leave empty for a plain backup with no credentials. Set one to also save Wi-Fi networks, SMB passwords and this account, encrypted.
backup.restoreConfirm: Restore this backup? A safety copy of the current configuration is taken first.
backup.deleteConfirm: Delete this backup? This cannot be undone.
backup.scheduledHint: Runs unattended, so it never includes credentials — only device settings, sources and Lyrion preferences/playlists.

system.rebootComingBack: Waiting for the device to come back online.
system.rebootAutoReconnect: This page will reconnect automatically — no need to refresh.
system.rebootTimeout: The device didn't come back online in time. Reload the page once it's back up.
system.supportBundleHint: Downloads a zip with device logs and system information, useful for diagnosing an issue remotely.
system.factoryHint: Factory reset erases all settings (networks, sources, DSP, Bluetooth, pairings) and this account, then restarts into initial setup. Confirm with the admin password.
system.factoryConfirm: This erases ALL settings and this account, then restarts into setup. Continue?
system.factoryStarted: Factory reset started — the device will restart

debug.bootHint: For a device that hangs at boot or shutdown behind the splash screen instead of failing cleanly — possibly a hidden kernel panic. Both settings need a reboot to take effect.
debug.plymouthHelp: Shows real boot/shutdown text instead of the graphical splash, so a hang or kernel panic is actually visible on the screen.
debug.kdump: Save a memory dump on kernel panic
debug.kdumpHelp: Reserves a small amount of RAM to capture the crash to disk (/var/crash) so it can be inspected after a kernel panic.
debug.kdumpNotInstalled: Installs the crash-dump tools the first time this is turned on (needs Internet access).
debug.rebootRequired: Saved — reboot the device for this to take effect.
debug.rebootPrompt: Reboot the device now to apply this?
